children: The NZX 50 was almost flat, trading around 13,657 in Tuesday morning deals, after losses in the previous two sessions, as gains in the tech and healthcare sectors were offset by declines in utilities and real estate.
Traders were cautious ahead of the release of Q3 inflation data due this week, which could guide the RBNZ's interest rate decision.

Caution also stemmed from rising oil prices, raising concerns about inflation and interest rate hikes amid escalating tensions in the Middle East. The broader index attempted to rebound from its lowest level since September 16, touched a day earlier, tracking an upbeat session on Wall Street overnight, supported by a rebound in the tech sector.
F&C Investment rose 1.8%, Infratil climbed 1.3%, Fisher & Paykel gained 0.6%, and Mainfreight increased 0.5%, while Mercury NZ dropped 0.7%, and ANZ Group and A2 Milk each fell 0.5%.

title: NZX 50 Little Changed in Morning Trade
